content.content:
1	"""Deterministic 2D grid A* planner.
2	
3	Public entry points: ``plan(width, height, blocked, start, goal, costs=None,
4	trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
5	max_cost=None, allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None)``,
6	``plan_any(width, height, blocked,
7	start, goals, costs=None, trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None,
8	max_expanded=None, snapshot=False, max_cost=None, allow_wait=False,
9	dynamic_costs=None)``,
10	``plan_k(width, height, blocked, start, goal, k, costs=None,
11	dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, max_cost=None,
12	allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None)``,
13	``plan_batch(width, height, blocked, requests, costs=None, trace=False,
14	dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
15	max_cost=None, allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None)``,
16	``plan_multi_start(width, height, blocked, starts, goal, costs=None,
17	trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
18	max_cost=None, allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None)``,
19	``replay(width, height, blocked, start, goal, path, costs=None,
20	dynamic_blocked=None, diagnose=False, allow_wait=False,
21	dynamic_costs=None)``,
22	``resume(checkpoint, max_expanded=None)``,
23	``distance_field(width, height, blocked, goal, costs=None, trace=False)``
24	and
25	``distance_field_any(width, height, blocked, goals, costs=None,
26	trace=False)``.
27	
28	Semantics:
29	- Four-neighborhood moves, Manhattan heuristic. Without ``costs`` each step
30	  has unit cost. With ``costs`` (a height-by-width matrix of positive
31	  integers, row-major: ``costs[y][x]``) entering a cell costs that cell's
32	  value; the start cell's cost is never counted, so ``cost`` is the sum of
33	  the costs of the cells entered along the path.
34	- Tie-breaking is fully specified and order-independent: compare f, then h,
35	  then the (x, y) coordinate in lexicographic order.
36	- ``expanded`` counts exactly the nodes popped from the priority queue and
37	  closed for the first time (the goal counts when reached; stale heap
38	  entries and duplicate closings do not).
39	- Returns ``{"path": [...], "cost": int, "expanded": int}`` on success and
40	  ``{"path": None, "cost": None, "expanded": int}`` when unreachable.
41	- When ``trace`` is true, both kinds of results additionally include
42	  ``expanded_nodes``: the list of coordinate tuples closed for the first
43	  time, in expansion order (includes the start, and the goal on success);
44	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``. The field is omitted entirely when
45	  ``trace`` is false or omitted.
46	
47	Search budget (``max_expanded``):
48	- ``max_expanded`` may be omitted or ``None``, which keeps every key,
49	  value, exception type and validation order of the default behavior
50	  untouched. Otherwise it must be a non-negative integer that is not a
51	  bool: other types raise ``TypeError`` and negative values raise
52	  ``ValueError``. These checks run after all existing grid, costs,
53	  ``trace`` and ``dynamic_blocked`` validation (including the frame-0
54	  check) and before the search starts.
55	- The budget counts closed nodes (exactly what ``expanded`` counts); once
56	  the limit is reached no further node is closed. When the budget is
57	  provided the result always carries an additional ``status`` field:
58	  ``"found"`` when the goal was closed within the limit (the usual
59	  ``path``/``cost`` are returned), ``"unreachable"`` when the candidates
60	  were exhausted without reaching the goal, and ``"budget_exhausted"``
61	  when live candidates remained but the budget stopped the search (then
62	  ``path``/``cost`` are ``None`` and ``expanded`` is the actual closed
63	  count, at most ``max_expanded``).
64	- The budget applies identically in static and dynamic mode and never
65	  changes expansion order, path choice, trace entries or determinism: a
66	  budgeted trace is a prefix of the unbudgeted one. With ``trace=True``
67	  only actually closed nodes are recorded, so a zero budget records
68	  nothing -- even when ``start == goal`` a zero budget returns
69	  ``budget_exhausted`` with ``expanded == 0``; the single-point success
70	  result requires at least one closed node (``max_expanded >= 1``).
71	- ``replay`` is unaffected: it keeps validating candidate paths only and
72	  accepts no budget parameter.
73	
74	Cost limit (``max_cost``):
75	- ``max_cost`` may be omitted or ``None``, which keeps every key, value,
76	  exception type and validation order of the previous behavior untouched.
77	  Otherwise it must be a non-negative integer that is not a bool: other
78	  types raise ``TypeError`` and negative values raise ``ValueError``. The
79	  check runs after all existing grid, costs, ``trace``, ``dynamic_blocked``,
80	  ``max_expanded`` and ``snapshot`` validation and before the search
81	  starts.
82	- The limit caps the accumulated entering-cell cost of a route, measured
83	  from the start (the start cell still costs 0 and each entered cell costs
84	  its ``costs`` value, or 1 without ``costs``). A candidate whose
85	  accumulated cost would exceed the limit is discarded; a candidate at
86	  exactly the limit still competes. The limit applies identically in
87	  static mode, dynamic mode and ``plan_any``, and never changes expansion
88	  order, tie-breaks, the minimum-cost choice, the multi-goal endpoint
89	  comparison or trace entries.
90	- When ``max_cost`` is provided the result always carries ``status``:
91	  ``"found"`` on success, and on failure ``"cost_exhausted"`` when at
92	  least one candidate was discarded for exceeding the limit, otherwise
93	  ``"unreachable"`` (``path``/``cost`` are ``None`` and ``expanded``
94	  counts the actually closed nodes). When ``max_expanded`` is also given,
95	  a budget stop still takes priority with ``"budget_exhausted"``.
96	  ``trace`` keeps recording only actually closed nodes, and the
97	  ``start == goal`` single-point zero-cost result and the zero-budget
98	  rules are unchanged.
99	- With ``snapshot=True`` the checkpoint records the ``max_cost`` value
100	  when one was provided (and no new field when it was not). ``resume``
101	  treats a checkpoint without the field as ``None``, validates a present
102	  field with the same rules (``TypeError`` for wrong types, ``ValueError``
103	  for negative values or a state inconsistent with the limit) before any
104	  searching, and a resumed search is equivalent to one uninterrupted call
105	  with the same limit. ``replay`` accepts no ``max_cost`` parameter.
106	
107	Waiting in place (``allow_wait``):
108	- ``plan``, ``plan_any``, ``plan_batch``, ``plan_multi_start``, ``plan_k``
109	  and ``replay`` accept a final optional boolean ``allow_wait`` that
110	  defaults to ``False``. ``False`` -- or an omitted, ``None`` or empty
111	  ``dynamic_blocked`` -- keeps every key, value, exception type,
112	  validation order, four-neighborhood move, no-repeated-coordinate rule
113	  and tie-break of the previous behavior untouched. A non-bool
114	  ``allow_wait`` raises ``TypeError`` after the ``dynamic_blocked``
115	  checks (the frame-0 check included) and before the budget and snapshot
116	  checks; every other exception type and order is unchanged.
117	- With ``allow_wait=True`` a route may stay in its current cell from
118	  time ``t`` to time ``t + 1`` provided the cell is not blocked at frame
119	  ``t + 1``. Waiting adds no entering-cell cost (``cost`` still sums
120	  only the cells entered by moves, and ``max_cost`` caps only those) and
121	  is only generated while ``t + 1`` lies within the provided frames:
122	  after the last frame the last frame is still reused for moves but no
123	  further waits are generated. Consecutive waits repeat the same
124	  coordinate in the path; once a cell is left it may never be
125	  re-entered. ``start == goal`` still yields only the single-point
126	  zero-cost route.
127	- The minimum-cost choice, the endpoint selection and the complete-path
128	  lexicographic tie-break follow the existing rules, with the priority
129	  still f, then h, then the coordinate, then the time and finally the
130	  complete path, so results never depend on obstacle-set or in-frame
131	  iteration order. Wait states count toward ``expanded`` one per closing
132	  and the trace records their ``(x, y, t)`` triples; ``max_expanded``
133	  truncates them like any other state and the ``status`` values and
134	  priorities are unchanged. ``plan_k``, ``plan_batch``, multi-goal and
135	  multi-start results follow the same waiting semantics, and a
136	  successful path verifies in ``replay`` with the same cost and step
137	  count, the waits included in ``steps``.
138	- ``replay`` with ``allow_wait=True`` accepts consecutive stays only
139	  within the provided dynamic frames; stays in static mode or without
140	  frames, stays after the final frame and non-consecutive revisits all
141	  return the usual invalid structure. With ``diagnose=True`` a stay
142	  after the final frame reports the dedicated error
143	  ``wait_after_final_frame``.
144	- A budget-exhausted checkpoint records ``allow_wait`` when it was true
145	  and ``resume`` of such a checkpoint is equivalent to one uninterrupted
146	  call with the same setting. Checkpoints written without the field
147	  restore it as ``False``; a present non-bool field raises ``TypeError``
148	  and a field inconsistent with the recorded internal state raises
149	  ``ValueError``.
150	
151	Dynamic obstacles (``dynamic_blocked``):
152	- ``dynamic_blocked`` may be omitted, ``None`` or an empty sequence, which
153	  leaves the static behavior above untouched. Otherwise it must be a
154	  sequence of frames; each frame is an iterable of grid coordinates that
155	  are blocked at that time frame. Frame 0 constrains ``start``; the
156	  coordinate at path index ``t`` must avoid both the static obstacles and
157	  frame ``t``, and frames beyond the last one reuse the last frame.
158	- Moves are still four-neighborhood only: no waiting in place and no
159	  repeated coordinates along the path. Because feasibility of a route
160	  depends on the coordinates it already visited, candidates that reach the
161	  same ``(x, y, t)`` through different coordinate histories are distinct
162	  states and are never merged: every route that satisfies the constraints
163	  can be explored. ``cost`` is still the sum of the costs of the cells
164	  entered; the start cell is never counted.
165	- The minimum-cost feasible route is returned. When total costs tie, the
166	  fixed priority is f, then h, then x, y, t, and candidates still tied are
167	  ordered lexicographically by their complete coordinate sequence, so the
168	  result never depends on the iteration order of the obstacle sets, the
169	  coordinates inside a frame, or the traversal order.
170	- In dynamic mode ``expanded_nodes`` records ``(x, y, t)`` triples in
171	  actual closing order and ``expanded`` counts closed space-time route
172	  states one per entry; a discarded candidate is never recorded. When the
173	  same ``(x, y, t)`` is closed through different histories, its triple
174	  appears once per closing in closing order, and ``expanded`` counts each
175	  such entry. On failure ``path``/``cost`` are ``None``.
176	- Validation: the outer value must be a sequence and every frame an
177	  iterable of coordinates; strings/bytes and non-two-integer coordinates
178	  raise ``TypeError``, out-of-bounds coordinates raise ``ValueError``,
179	  duplicates within a frame are merged, and a ``start`` blocked at frame 0
180	  raises ``ValueError``. All checks run before the search starts.
181	
182	Time-varying costs (``dynamic_costs``):
183	- ``plan``, ``plan_any``, ``plan_batch``, ``plan_multi_start``,
184	  ``plan_k`` and ``replay`` accept a final optional
185	  ``dynamic_costs=None`` parameter. Omitting it, passing ``None`` or an
186	  empty sequence keeps every result key, exception boundary, expansion
187	  order, path choice and the legacy ``costs`` semantics of the previous
188	  behavior untouched; every other entry point keeps its signature.
189	- Otherwise ``dynamic_costs`` must be a sequence of height-by-width
190	  matrices of positive integers, one matrix per time frame. An outer
191	  value or frame that is not an acceptable sequence, or a cell that is
192	  not a non-bool integer, raises ``TypeError``; a wrong row or column
193	  count, a non-positive cost, or providing both ``costs`` and
194	  ``dynamic_costs`` raises ``ValueError``. All checks run after every
195	  pre-existing validation (in ``plan_batch`` before any request is
196	  searched) and before the search starts.
197	- When enabled, entering a coordinate at path index ``t`` costs that
198	  cell's value in frame ``t``; the start cell is still never charged and
199	  frames beyond the last one reuse the last frame. Waiting follows the
200	  existing rules and never produces an entering-cell cost. The search
201	  returns the globally minimum total ``cost`` route under the static and
202	  dynamic obstacle constraints; equal costs are still arbitrated by the
203	  existing endpoint and complete-path lexicographic rules, and
204	  ``expanded``/``expanded_nodes`` count only actually closed space-time
205	  states: distinct histories are never merged and no out-of-bounds,
206	  blocked or illegally repeated nodes are generated.
207	- ``max_cost`` caps the dynamic accumulated cost with the usual
208	  ``cost_exhausted`` and budget-priority rules; ``plan_any``'s winning
209	  endpoint rules, the trace shape, the ``start == goal`` result and
210	  unreachable results are unchanged. ``plan_batch`` answers each
211	  request exactly as an independent ``plan`` call with the same frames;
212	  ``plan_multi_start`` picks its winner by the same total-cost and
213	  complete-path tie-breaks and records ``(x, y, t)`` trace triples in
214	  dynamic mode; ``plan_k`` ranks its unique routes by the dynamic
215	  accumulated cost with the usual truncation and status rules.
216	  ``replay`` recomputes ``cost``
217	  with the same frames, so a legal path matches the planning result;
218	  the diagnostic error types and the ``steps`` rule are unchanged.
219	- With ``snapshot=True`` the checkpoint records ``dynamic_costs`` as a
220	  JSON-serializable structure (the field is omitted when they were not
221	  provided) together with the waiting setting, the accumulated state and
222	  the cost limit when one was provided; a resumed search matches one
223	  uninterrupted call field by field, the next checkpoint included. A
224	  checkpoint whose ``dynamic_costs`` is corrupt raises ``TypeError`` or
225	  ``ValueError`` and never silently degrades. ``plan_k`` accepts no
226	  snapshot option.
227	
228	Multi-goal planning (``plan_any``):
229	- ``plan_any(width, height, blocked, start, goals, ...)`` accepts the same
230	  grid, blocked, start, costs, trace, dynamic_blocked and max_expanded
231	  arguments as ``plan``, plus a non-empty ``goals`` sequence of candidate
232	  endpoint coordinates. It returns one deterministic minimum-cost route to
233	  any of the candidates, in the same result structure as ``plan``; the
234	  path's last point is the winning endpoint.
235	- The grid, costs, trace, dynamic-blocked and budget checks run in
236	  ``plan``'s order with the same exception types; ``goals`` takes
237	  ``goal``'s position in that sequence. The outer value must be a
238	  sequence: strings, bytes, ``None`` and other non-sequences raise
239	  ``TypeError`` and an empty sequence raises ``ValueError``. Each endpoint
240	  follows the coordinate structure and integer rules (bad shape or
241	  coordinate types raise ``TypeError``); out-of-bounds coordinates and
242	  endpoints on static obstacles raise ``ValueError``. Repeated candidates
243	  merge, so the input ordering never changes any result.
244	- The search keeps four-neighborhood moves, no waiting, no revisits, the
245	  persistent last frame and the entering-cell cost accumulation. A
246	  candidate blocked by the dynamic frame at the time a particular route
247	  arrives is not rejected up front (its coordinate is statically valid);
248	  that arrival is simply infeasible for that route's time frame while
249	  other arrival times still compete.
250	- Total ``cost`` decides; ties compare the endpoint coordinate ``(x, y)``
251	  lexicographically, then the complete coordinate path lexicographically.
252	  As in dynamic ``plan``, routes reaching the same cell through different
253	  coordinate histories are distinct states and are never merged, so the
254	  traversal is a best-first walk of the feasible route tree; expansion
255	  order and the trace never depend on goal order, the blocked sets or
256	  in-frame iteration order. A budget never replaces an already determined
257	  better route with a worse one.
258	- When no endpoint is reachable, ``path`` and ``cost`` are ``None``. With a
259	  budget the ``status`` field follows the same ``"found"``,
260	  ``"unreachable"`` and ``"budget_exhausted"`` rules, and ``trace`` only
261	  records actually closed nodes: coordinate pairs in static mode and
262	  ``(x, y, t)`` triples in dynamic mode. A ``goals`` containing ``start``
263	  yields the single-point zero-cost route under the same start-equals-goal
264	  and zero-budget rules as ``plan``. A successful path verifies offline in
265	  ``replay`` when its last point is passed as ``goal``, with the same cost
266	  and step count.
267	
268	Top-k planning (``plan_k``):
269	- ``plan_k(width, height, blocked, start, goal, k, costs=None,
270	  dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, max_cost=None,
271	  allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None)`` returns
272	  several distinct feasible routes on the same grid in one call. It
273	  first performs exactly ``plan``'s shared validation for the
274	  dimensions, coordinates, static obstacles, positive integer cost
275	  matrix and dynamic frames (including the frame-0 start check), and
276	  only then checks ``k``: a non-bool positive integer is required,
277	  wrong types raise ``TypeError`` and non-positive values raise
278	  ``ValueError``. The optional ``max_expanded`` and ``max_cost``
279	  limits are checked after all of that (the ``k`` check included),
280	  still before the search starts, with the same non-negative,
281	  non-bool integer rules ``plan`` uses (other types raise
282	  ``TypeError``, negative values raise ``ValueError``). The optional
283	  ``dynamic_costs`` frames are validated after all of those checks,
284	  still before the search starts, with the shared time-varying cost
285	  rules (providing both ``costs`` and ``dynamic_costs`` raises
286	  ``ValueError``). Every error is
287	  decided before the search starts, and ``plan_k`` accepts no
288	  ``trace`` or ``snapshot`` argument.
289	- The search keeps four-neighborhood moves, the zero start cost, the
290	  entering-cell cost accumulation, the persistent last frame, the ban on
291	  waiting in place and on repeated coordinates, and the static/frame
292	  feasibility rules. Routes that reach the same cell through different
293	  coordinate histories are distinct candidates and are never merged, in
294	  both static and dynamic mode, so different complete coordinate
295	  sequences always remain separate results.
296	- It returns ``{"paths": [...], "costs": [...], "expanded": int}``: at
297	  most ``k`` unique complete routes ordered by ascending total cost and,
298	  on ties, by the lexicographic order of the complete coordinate
299	  sequence; ``costs`` corresponds to ``paths`` entry by entry. The first
300	  entry is the route ``plan`` would return. When no route is feasible
301	  both lists are empty and ``expanded`` still reports the route
302	  candidates actually closed to determine the answer: one count per
303	  complete history, and never counting a candidate filtered at
304	  generation or left pending. The traversal stops the moment the k-th
305	  goal route has been closed, so a small k closes strictly fewer
306	  candidates than a larger one. ``start == goal`` yields only the
307	  single-point zero-cost route, with one expansion. Every returned route
308	  verifies offline in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count, in
309	  both static and dynamic mode; the result never depends on obstacle-set
310	  iteration order, in-frame coordinate order or the traversal order.
311	- ``max_cost`` caps a route's accumulated entering-cell cost exactly as
312	  in ``plan``: the start still costs 0, a candidate exactly at the
313	  limit still competes and a candidate whose accumulated cost would
314	  exceed it is discarded the moment it is generated. It never changes
315	  the tie-break between legal routes. ``max_expanded`` caps the number
316	  of complete route candidates actually closed (exactly what
317	  ``expanded`` counts); once the limit is reached no further candidate
318	  is closed, and the limit only ever truncates the traversal -- it can
319	  never replace an already determined higher-ranked route. When either
320	  limit is provided the result additionally carries ``status``:
321	  ``"found"`` when all ``k`` routes were closed or the search exhausted
322	  naturally with at least one route; ``"budget_exhausted"`` when fewer
323	  than ``k`` routes were found and the budget stopped the search while
324	  candidates were still pending (this wins when both limits fire);
325	  ``"cost_exhausted"`` when fewer than ``k`` routes were found, no
326	  budget stop occurred and at least one candidate was discarded for the
327	  cost limit; ``"unreachable"`` when no route exists with neither a
328	  budget stop nor a cost discard. The routes already closed (and their
329	  costs, in rank order) are still returned when a limit ends the search
330	  early, as empty lists when none were found, and ``expanded`` is the
331	  actual closed count. Omitting both limits keeps every legacy key and
332	  value exactly unchanged.
333	
334	Batch planning (``plan_batch``):
335	- ``plan_batch(width, height, blocked, requests, costs=None,
336	  trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
337	  max_cost=None, allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None)`` answers
338	  several independent single-goal queries on
339	  one shared grid in a single call. It returns ``{"results": [...]}``
340	  with exactly the result ``plan`` would return for each query, in the
341	  order of ``requests``; duplicate requests are kept and each gets its
342	  own result.
343	- The shared arguments are validated with ``plan``'s rules and order,
344	  with ``requests`` taking the position of ``start``/``goal`` in that
345	  sequence. ``requests`` must be a non-empty sequence: ``None``,
346	  strings, bytes and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError`` and an
347	  empty sequence raises ``ValueError``. Each element must be a
348	  two-element sequence ``[start, goal]`` of grid coordinates: element
349	  shape or coordinate type failures raise ``TypeError``; out-of-bounds
350	  coordinates, endpoints on static obstacles and a start blocked at
351	  dynamic frame 0 raise ``ValueError``. Every check is decided before
352	  any search starts, so an invalid batch never returns partial results.
353	- Each query is an independent ``plan`` search over the shared grid:
354	  ``path``, ``cost`` and ``expanded`` are produced per request, and the
355	  ``max_expanded`` budget and the ``max_cost`` limit apply per query
356	  with no state shared across queries. The optional ``dynamic_costs``
357	  frames follow the shared time-varying cost rules and are validated
358	  after every other check, before any request is searched; each request
359	  is then answered exactly as an independent ``plan`` call with the
360	  same frames, and a per-request checkpoint records them. ``trace``,
361	  ``status``,
362	  ``expanded_nodes``, ``checkpoint``, dynamic frames, ``start == goal``,
363	  unreachable and ``cost_exhausted`` results all follow ``plan``
364	  exactly, and a returned ``checkpoint`` can be handed to ``resume``
365	  directly. A successful path ends at its request's goal and verifies
366	  offline in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count. The result
367	  never depends on obstacle-set iteration order, in-frame coordinate
368	  order or the permutation of ``requests``.
369	
370	Multi-start planning (``plan_multi_start``):
371	- ``plan_multi_start(width, height, blocked, starts, goal, costs=None,
372	  trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
373	  max_cost=None, allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None)`` plans from
374	  several candidate starts to one shared
375	  goal in a single call and returns one deterministic route, in exactly
376	  the result structure of ``plan``; the path begins at the winning start
377	  and ends at ``goal``. ``starts`` takes ``start``'s position in
378	  ``plan``'s validation sequence and every shared check keeps its order,
379	  exception type and message boundary.
380	- ``starts`` must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates: ``None``,
381	  strings, bytes and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError`` and an
382	  empty sequence raises ``ValueError``. Each start follows the
383	  coordinate structure and integer rules (bad shape or coordinate types
384	  raise ``TypeError``); out-of-bounds coordinates and starts on static
385	  obstacles raise ``ValueError``. Repeated starts merge and the tuple is
386	  sorted, so the input ordering never changes any result. A start
387	  blocked by dynamic frame 0 raises ``ValueError``; every check runs
388	  before the search starts.
389	- In static mode every start is a ``g == 0`` root and each coordinate is
390	  closed at most once: a cell keeps only its best known ``(cost, path)``
391	  pair (smallest accumulated entering-cell cost, then the
392	  lexicographically smallest complete coordinate sequence -- an ordering
393	  preserved under common extensions, so a dominated candidate can never
394	  win later). In dynamic mode the persistent last frame, the ban on
395	  waiting and on repeated coordinates apply, and routes reaching the
396	  same ``(x, y, t)`` through different coordinate histories are distinct
397	  states that are never merged. Time-varying ``dynamic_costs`` frames
398	  (validated after every other check, before the search) make the
399	  search time-expanded the same way obstacle frames do: entering a
400	  coordinate at path index ``t`` costs that frame's cell value, the
401	  last frame persists, and the trace records ``(x, y, t)`` triples.
402	- The winning route has the smallest total ``cost``; ties are decided by
403	  the lexicographic order of the complete coordinate path, so the result
404	  never depends on the input order of ``starts``. Expansion order is f,
405	  then h, then ``(x, y)`` (plus ``t`` in dynamic mode), and finally the
406	  complete path. ``cost`` counts only the cells entered (the winning
407	  start costs 0); ``expanded`` counts only closed candidates; when no
408	  route exists ``path`` and ``cost`` are ``None``.
409	- With ``trace=True`` static mode records the unique coordinate closing
410	  sequence and dynamic mode the ``(x, y, t)`` closing sequence, and
411	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``. A ``starts`` entry equal to
412	  ``goal`` yields the single-point zero-cost route under the same
413	  start-equals-goal and zero-budget rules as ``plan``.
414	- ``max_expanded`` and ``max_cost`` follow ``plan``'s ``status`` and
415	  budget-priority rules: a candidate whose accumulated cost would
416	  exceed ``max_cost`` is discarded without counting toward ``expanded``,
417	  and neither limit ever changes the unlimited route or the tie-breaks.
418	  With ``snapshot=True`` a budget stop returns a JSON-serializable
419	  checkpoint recording the sorted starts, the grid constraints, the
420	  dynamic frames, the time-varying cost frames when they were provided,
421	  the cost limit when one was provided and the complete
422	  pending state; ``resume`` continues it with the cumulative-budget,
423	  no-double-counting and only-budget-exhausted-snapshots rules of the
424	  other planners, and invalid checkpoints follow ``resume``'s usual
425	  ``TypeError``/``ValueError`` boundaries.
426	
427	Snapshots and resumable planning (``snapshot`` and ``resume``):
428	- ``plan`` and ``plan_any`` accept a final ``snapshot=False`` option.
429	  Omitting it or passing ``False`` keeps every key, value, exception type,
430	  validation order, tie-break, unreachable result and trace of the
431	  previous behavior untouched. A non-bool ``snapshot`` raises
432	  ``TypeError`` after all existing checks (the ``max_expanded`` validation
433	  included) and before the search starts.
434	- With ``snapshot=True``, a search that stops because ``max_expanded``
435	  was reached (``status == "budget_exhausted"``) additionally returns
436	  ``checkpoint``: a fully JSON-serializable snapshot of the planner state.
437	  Results that already found the goal or proved it unreachable never
438	  carry the field.
439	- The checkpoint records the snapshot version, the planner kind, the
440	  normalized grid constraints (dimensions, obstacles, start, goal or
441	  candidate goals, costs, dynamic frames and the cost limit when one was
442	  provided), the closed-node count, the
443	  trace recorded so far and the complete pending-candidate state. Every
444	  set-derived list is stored sorted, so neither obstacle-set iteration
445	  order, goal order nor in-frame coordinate order influences the
446	  checkpoint's keys or values. A caller may store it as-is and hand it
447	  back to ``resume`` later.
448	- ``resume(checkpoint, max_expanded=None)`` continues the very same
449	  deterministic search described by the snapshot. ``max_expanded`` keeps
450	  its cumulative meaning: the total number of nodes that may be closed
451	  counted from the original start, so a limit not greater than the
452	  already closed count closes nothing more. The result is equivalent to
453	  one uninterrupted call with the same cumulative budget: ``path``,
454	  ``cost``, ``expanded``, ``status`` (present exactly when
455	  ``max_expanded`` is given) and ``expanded_nodes`` (always present in
456	  resume results; coordinate pairs in static mode, ``(x, y, t)`` triples
457	  in dynamic mode) all match, and repeated resumes never count an already
458	  closed node twice.
459	- When a resumed search reaches the budget again its result carries a
460	  fresh ``checkpoint`` that can be resumed in turn; ``found`` and
461	  ``unreachable`` results omit it. A successful resumed ``path`` verifies
462	  in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count.
463	- Validation: a checkpoint that is not an object, has missing required
464	  fields or wrongly typed fields raises ``TypeError``; an unsupported
465	  snapshot version or planner kind, grid constraints that violate the
466	  usual ``plan`` rules (obstacles, endpoints, costs, dynamic frames) or
467	  an internally inconsistent state raise ``ValueError``. Every check is
468	  decided before any searching, and ``resume``'s ``max_expanded`` follows
469	  the same non-negative-integer rules as ``plan``'s.
470	
471	Offline replay (``replay``):
472	- ``replay`` re-checks a saved candidate path without running any search;
473	  it never returns ``expanded`` or ``expanded_nodes``. It accepts the same
474	  grid arguments as ``plan`` (no ``trace``) plus ``path``.
475	- The grid arguments are validated with exactly the public ``plan``
476	  checks, and all of them run before the path is judged, so the same
477	  malformed grid inputs raise the same ``TypeError``/``ValueError``.
478	- ``path`` must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates; strings,
479	  bytes, ``None`` and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError``, as do
480	  elements that are not exactly two integers. Coordinates outside the
481	  grid raise ``ValueError``.
482	- A structurally valid but semantically invalid path does not raise: it
483	  returns ``{"valid": False, "cost": None, "steps": None}`` with no
484	  partial accumulation. Invalid means: not beginning at ``start``, not
485	  ending at ``goal``, visiting a static obstacle, visiting a cell blocked
486	  by frame ``t`` at path index ``t`` (the last frame persists for later
487	  indices; omitted/empty ``dynamic_blocked`` means static-only checks),
488	  non-four-neighbor adjacency, repeated coordinates, or extra points when
489	  ``start == goal``.
490	- A valid path returns ``{"valid": True, "cost": int, "steps": int}``
491	  where ``steps == len(path) - 1`` and ``cost`` is recomputed with the
492	  same entering-cell rule ``plan`` uses (sum of the costs of the cells
493	  entered; unit costs without ``costs``; the start cell is never
494	  counted), so it equals the cost ``plan`` assigns to that same path.
495	- ``diagnose`` defaults to false; omitting it or passing ``False`` keeps
496	  every key, value, exception type and validation order identical. A
497	  non-bool ``diagnose`` raises ``TypeError`` after all grid checks
498	  (including the frame-0 check) and before the path structure is
499	  inspected. With ``diagnose=True`` both results additionally carry
500	  ``error`` and ``error_index``: ``None``/``None`` for a valid path, and
501	  for an invalid one a single error code plus the zero-based index of
502	  the first offending element, with ``cost``/``steps`` still ``None``.
503	  The codes, in fixed precedence order, are ``start_mismatch`` (index
504	  0), ``goal_mismatch`` (index of the last element),
505	  ``start_goal_extra`` (index 1), ``repeated_coordinate`` (the second
506	  occurrence), ``non_adjacent`` (the later element of the pair),
507	  ``static_blocked`` and ``dynamic_blocked`` (the offending element);
508	  ties resolve to the earliest rule in this list and no partial cost is
509	  ever returned.
510	
511	Distance field (``distance_field``):
512	- ``distance_field(width, height, blocked, goal, costs=None,
513	  trace=False)`` is an offline analysis entry point for the static grid:
514	  it accepts only the dimensions, the static obstacles, a single goal and
515	  optionally ``costs`` and ``trace`` -- no start, no dynamic obstacles, no
516	  search budget, no cost limit and no snapshot option. The dimensions,
517	  goal coordinate, obstacle and costs checks (structure, integer types,
518	  bounds, duplicate merging, goal-on-obstacle) follow ``plan``'s public
519	  rules and order for those shared arguments and all run before the
520	  search starts; ``trace`` must be a bool (``TypeError`` otherwise).
521	- It returns ``{"distances": ..., "expanded": int}`` where ``distances``
522	  is a height-by-width matrix indexed ``distances[y][x]``: ``None`` for
523	  obstacles and for cells that cannot reach the goal, ``0`` for the goal
524	  itself, and for every other reachable cell the minimum sum of the
525	  entering-cell costs along a four-neighborhood route from that cell to
526	  the goal (unit steps without ``costs``; with ``costs`` each move adds
527	  the cost of the cell entered, exactly as ``plan`` accumulates ``cost``,
528	  so a reachable ``plan`` start yields the same value ``plan`` reports
529	  as ``cost``). No reachable distance is ever negative and the matrix
530	  always matches the grid dimensions; the result is JSON-serializable.
531	- ``expanded`` counts exactly the reachable cells determined and closed
532	  once each, the goal included. The closing order is fully specified:
533	  smallest current distance first, then the ``(x, y)`` coordinate in
534	  lexicographic order, so neither the obstacle-set iteration order nor
535	  the costs layout traversal influences the matrix, the count or the
536	  trace. With ``trace=True`` the result additionally carries
537	  ``expanded_nodes``, the coordinate pairs in that closing order, and
538	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``; the field is omitted entirely
539	  when ``trace`` is false or omitted.
540	
541	Multi-goal distance field (``distance_field_any``):
542	- ``distance_field_any(width, height, blocked, goals, costs=None,
543	  trace=False)`` is the multi-goal counterpart of ``distance_field``:
544	  one offline analysis returns the minimum-cost field to any of the
545	  candidate endpoints in a single pass. It accepts only the dimensions,
546	  the static obstacles, a non-empty ``goals`` sequence and optionally
547	  ``costs`` and ``trace`` -- no start, no dynamic obstacles, no search
548	  budget, no cost limit and no snapshot option, and it never produces a
549	  ``status`` field. The dimensions, obstacles, costs and trace checks
550	  follow ``distance_field``'s public rules and order, and ``goals`` is
551	  validated exactly like ``plan_any``'s: ``None``, strings, bytes and
552	  other non-sequences raise ``TypeError``, an empty sequence raises
553	  ``ValueError``, elements that are not exactly two non-bool integers
554	  raise ``TypeError``, and out-of-bounds coordinates or endpoints on
555	  static obstacles raise ``ValueError``. The goals checks occupy
556	  ``goal``'s position in ``distance_field``'s validation sequence,
557	  duplicates merge, and every check runs before the search starts, so
558	  the input permutation never changes any result.
559	- It returns ``{"distances": ..., "targets": ..., "expanded": int}``.
560	  ``distances`` is the same height-by-width matrix as
561	  ``distance_field``: ``None`` for obstacles and for cells that cannot
562	  reach any endpoint, ``0`` for every endpoint, and otherwise the
563	  minimum over the endpoints of the accumulated entering-cell cost
564	  along a four-neighborhood route (unit steps without ``costs``; with
565	  ``costs`` each move adds the cost of the cell entered, the start
566	  cell's own cost never counted, exactly as ``plan``/``plan_any`` and
567	  ``distance_field`` accumulate). A reachable ``plan_any`` start yields
568	  the same value ``plan_any`` reports as ``cost``.
569	- ``targets`` is a matrix of the same shape: a reachable cell records
570	  the coordinate tuple of the endpoint that wins it, every other
571	  position is ``None`` (obstacles and unreachable cells, exactly where
572	  ``distances`` is ``None``); endpoints record themselves. When several
573	  endpoints tie at the same minimum distance the winner is the endpoint
574	  with the lexicographically smallest ``(x, y)`` coordinate, so the
575	  choice never depends on goal order. The whole result is
576	  JSON-serializable.
577	- ``expanded`` counts every reachable cell closed for the first time,
578	  all endpoints included, exactly once each. The closing order is
579	  smallest distance first, then the ``(x, y)`` coordinate
580	  lexicographically. With ``trace=True`` the result additionally
581	  carries ``expanded_nodes`` -- the coordinate pairs in that order,
582	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)`` -- and the key is omitted
583	  entirely when ``trace`` is false or omitted.
584	
585	Validation (all performed before the search starts):
586	- ``width``/``height`` must be positive integers.
587	- ``start``, ``goal`` and every entry of ``blocked`` must be grid
588	  coordinates: sequences of exactly two integers (tuples, lists, etc.),
589	  normalized to tuples.
590	- ``goals`` (``plan_any`` and ``distance_field_any``) must be a
591	  non-empty sequence of grid coordinates following the same rules,
592	  normalized, deduplicated and order-independent.
593	- ``requests`` (``plan_batch``) must be a non-empty sequence of
594	  two-element ``[start, goal]`` coordinate pairs following the same
595	  coordinate rules, with the input order and duplicates preserved.
596	- ``costs`` may be omitted or ``None`` (unit costs). Otherwise it must be a
597	  sequence of ``height`` rows, each a sequence of ``width`` positive
598	  integers; strings/bytes, non-integer cells and booleans are rejected.
599	- ``dynamic_costs`` (``plan``, ``plan_any``, ``plan_batch``,
600	  ``plan_multi_start``, ``plan_k`` and ``replay``) may be
601	  omitted, ``None`` or an empty sequence. Otherwise it must be a
602	  sequence of frames, each frame a height-by-width matrix following the
603	  ``costs`` rules per frame; providing both ``costs`` and
604	  ``dynamic_costs`` raises ``ValueError``.
605	- ``trace`` must be a bool; non-bool values raise ``TypeError``.
606	- Type or structure violations raise ``TypeError``; non-positive
607	  dimensions, out-of-bounds coordinates, endpoints on obstacles, wrong
608	  matrix shape, or non-positive cell costs raise ``ValueError``.
609	- Duplicate blocked cells are merged without changing the result.
610	"""

626	def _is_int(value):
627	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)

630	def _validate_dimension(value, name):
631	    if not _is_int(value):
632	        raise TypeError(
633	            f"{name} must be an int, got {type(value).__name__}"
634	        )
635	    if value <= 0:

640	def _normalize_point(value, name):
641	    if isinstance(value, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(value, Sequence):
642	        raise TypeError(
643	            f"{name} must be a sequence of two integers, "
644	            f"got {type(value).__name__}"
645	        )
646	    if len(value) != 2:
647	        raise TypeError(
648	            f"{name} must contain exactly two coordinates, got {len(value)}"
649	        )
650	    x, y = value[0], value[1]
651	    if not _is_int(x) or not _is_int(y):
652	        raise TypeError(f"{name} coordinates must be integers, got {value!r}")
653	    return (x, y)

656	def _check_bounds(point, width, height, name):
657	    x, y = point
658	    if not (0 <= x < width and 0 <= y < height):
659	        raise ValueError(

664	def _normalize_blocked(blocked, width, height):
665	    if isinstance(blocked, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(blocked, Iterable):
666	        raise TypeError(
667	            f"blocked must be an iterable of grid coordinates, "
668	            f"got {type(blocked).__name__}"
669	        )
670	    cells = set()
671	    for index, item in enumerate(blocked):
672	        name = f"blocked[{index}]"
673	        point = _normalize_point(item, name)
674	        _check_bounds(point, width, height, name)
675	        cells.add(point)  # duplicates merge into one cell

679	def _normalize_costs(costs, width, height):
680	    if costs is None:
681	        return None  # unit step cost
682	    if isinstance(costs, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(costs, Sequence):
683	        raise TypeError(
684	            f"costs must be a height-by-width matrix of positive integers, "
685	            f"got {type(costs).__name__}"
686	        )
687	    if len(costs) != height:
688	        raise ValueError(
689	            f"costs must have exactly {height} rows, got {len(costs)}"
690	        )
691	    rows = []
692	    for y, row in enumerate(costs):
693	        if isinstance(row, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(row, Sequence):
694	            raise TypeError(
695	                f"costs[{y}] must be a sequence of {width} positive "
696	                f"integers, got {type(row).__name__}"
697	            )
698	        if len(row) != width:
699	            raise ValueError(
700	                f"costs[{y}] must have exactly {width} cells, "
701	                f"got {len(row)}"
702	            )
703	        parsed = []
704	        for x, cell in enumerate(row):
705	            if not _is_int(cell):
706	                raise TypeError(
707	                    f"costs[{y}][{x}] must be an int, "
708	                    f"got {type(cell).__name__}"
709	                )
710	            if cell <= 0:
711	                raise ValueError(
712	                    f"costs[{y}][{x}] must be a positive integer, "
713	                    f"got {cell}"
714	                )
715	            parsed.append(cell)
716	        rows.append(tuple(parsed))
717	    return tuple(rows)

981	def _search_static(width, height, obstacles, start, goal, costs, trace,
982	                   max_expanded, max_cost=None, snapshot=False,
983	                   allow_wait=False, state=None):
984	    """Classic static-grid A* (the ``plan`` search without frames).
985	
986	    Cells are merged by coordinate: the best known ``g`` per cell is kept
987	    in ``g_score``, stale heap entries are skipped, and ``came_from``
988	    reconstructs the cheapest route once the goal is closed. With
989	    ``max_cost`` a candidate whose accumulated entering-cell cost would
990	    exceed the limit is discarded instead of queued, and the search
991	    remembers whether any discard happened (``cost_limited``) so a
992	    failure can be reported as ``cost_exhausted``; the flag is part of
993	    the snapshot state so a resumed search stays equivalent to one
994	    uninterrupted call. With
995	    ``snapshot=True`` a budget stop additionally returns a checkpoint of
996	    the complete search state; ``state`` carries such a snapshot back in
997	    so ``resume`` continues the identical traversal. The snapshot needs
998	    the trace even when the caller did not ask for it, so nodes are
999	    recorded whenever ``trace`` or ``snapshot`` is true.
1000	    """
1001	
1002	    def heuristic(point):
1003	        return abs(point[0] - goal[0]) + abs(point[1] - goal[1])
1004	
1005	    def step_cost(point):
1006	        # Cost of entering ``point``; the start cell is never entered.
1007	        if costs is None:
1008	            return 1
1009	        return costs[point[1]][point[0]]
1010	
1011	    if state is None:
1012	        # Heap entries are (f, h, x, y, point): the first four fields give
1013	        # a total, input-order-independent ordering, so the point itself
1014	        # is never compared.
1015	        h0 = heuristic(start)
1016	        open_heap = [(h0, h0, start[0], start[1], start)]
1017	        came_from = {}
1018	        g_score = {start: 0}
1019	        closed = set()
1020	        expanded_nodes = [] if trace or snapshot else None
1021	        cost_limited = False
1022	    else:
1023	        open_heap = state["open"]
1024	        came_from = state["came_from"]
1025	        g_score = state["g_score"]
1026	        closed = state["closed"]
1027	        expanded_nodes = state["expanded_nodes"]
1028	        cost_limited = state["cost_limited"]
1029	    budget_stop = False
1030	    has_status = max_expanded is not None or max_cost is not None
1031	
1032	    while open_heap:
1033	        entry = heapq.heappop(open_heap)
1034	        current = entry[4]
1035	        if current in closed:
1036	            continue  # stale heap entry; already closed with its best g
1037	        if max_expanded is not None and len(closed) >= max_expanded:
1038	            # A live candidate remains but the budget is spent; close
1039	            # nothing more (this also covers start == goal with a zero
1040	            # budget: no node is closed and no start is fabricated). The
1041	            # popped candidate was already removed from the heap, so for a
1042	            # snapshot it is pushed back: the checkpoint must hold every
1043	            # still-live candidate for the search to resume exactly.
1044	            budget_stop = True
1045	            if snapshot:
1046	                heapq.heappush(open_heap, entry)
1047	            break
1048	        closed.add(current)
1049	        if expanded_nodes is not None:
1050	            expanded_nodes.append(current)
1051	        if current == goal:
1052	            path = [current]
1053	            while path[-1] in came_from:
1054	                path.append(came_from[path[-1]])
1055	            path.reverse()
1056	            result = {
1057	                "path": path,
1058	                "cost": g_score[current],
1059	                "expanded": len(closed),
1060	            }
1061	            if has_status:
1062	                result["status"] = "found"
1063	            if trace:
1064	                result["expanded_nodes"] = expanded_nodes
1065	            return result
1066	        for dx, dy in _NEIGHBORS:
1067	            nxt = (current[0] + dx, current[1] + dy)
1068	            if not (0 <= nxt[0] < width and 0 <= nxt[1] < height):
1069	                continue
1070	            if nxt in obstacles:
1071	                continue
1072	            new_g = g_score[current] + step_cost(nxt)
1073	            if new_g < g_score.get(nxt, float("inf")):
1074	                if max_cost is not None and new_g > max_cost:
1075	                    # The candidate's accumulated cost exceeds the limit:
1076	                    # discard it and remember that a discard happened.
1077	                    cost_limited = True
1078	                    continue
1079	                g_score[nxt] = new_g
1080	                came_from[nxt] = current
1081	                h = heuristic(nxt)
1082	                heapq.heappush(
1083	                    open_heap, (new_g + h, h, nxt[0], nxt[1], nxt)
1084	                )
1085	    result = {"path": None, "cost": None, "expanded": len(closed)}
1086	    if has_status:
1087	        result["status"] = _status_for(budget_stop, cost_limited)
1088	    if trace:
1089	        result["expanded_nodes"] = expanded_nodes
1090	    if snapshot and result.get("status") == "budget_exhausted":
1091	        result["checkpoint"] = _snapshot_checkpoint(
1092	            "plan", width, height, obstacles, start, goal, costs, None,
1093	            max_cost, len(closed), expanded_nodes,
1094	            _static_snapshot_state(open_heap, came_from, g_score, closed,
1095	                                   cost_limited, max_cost),
1096	            allow_wait,
1097	        )
1098	    return result

1101	def _search_dynamic(width, height, obstacles, frames, start, goal, costs,
1102	                    trace, max_expanded, max_cost=None, snapshot=False,
1103	                    allow_wait=False, state=None, cost_frames=None):
1104	    """History-sensitive time-expanded A*.
1105	
1106	    Frame ``t`` constrains the cell occupied at path index ``t``; frames
1107	    past the last one reuse the last frame. ``frames`` may be ``None``
1108	    when ``cost_frames`` is given: time-varying costs alone already make
1109	    the search space time-expanded. With ``cost_frames`` the price of
1110	    entering a cell at time ``t`` is that frame's cell value (frames past
1111	    the last one reuse the last frame); the start cell is never counted.
1112	    Waiting in place (unless ``allow_wait`` is set) and repeated
1113	    coordinates are forbidden, so
1114	    whether a candidate route can be
1115	    extended depends on the exact sequence of cells it already visited:
1116	    two routes reaching the same ``(x, y, t)`` with different histories
1117	    are distinct states and neither may prune the other (the route with
1118	    the larger accumulated cost can be the only one that remains
1119	    extendable). Each heap node therefore carries its complete path; the
1120	    search is a best-first traversal of the feasible route tree. Goal
1121	    closings are collected until the heap's smallest f exceeds the best
1122	    goal cost, after which the minimum-cost goal tie-break is settled by
1123	    the fixed f, h, x, y, t priority and then the complete path's
1124	    lexicographic order. With ``max_cost`` a candidate route whose
1125	    accumulated entering-cell cost would exceed the limit is discarded
1126	    (``cost_limited`` records that any discard happened, so a failure can
1127	    be reported as ``cost_exhausted``; the flag is part of the snapshot
1128	    state). With ``allow_wait`` a route may also stay in its current cell
1129	    for one frame at no entering-cell cost, generated only while the next
1130	    time step still lies within the provided frames and the cell is free
1131	    there; consecutive waits repeat the coordinate in the path, and once
1132	    a cell is left it may never be re-entered. With ``snapshot=True`` a
1133	    budget stop additionally
1134	    returns a checkpoint of the complete route-tree state; ``state``
1135	    carries such a snapshot back in for ``resume``.
1136	    """
1137	
1138	    def heuristic(point):
1139	        return abs(point[0] - goal[0]) + abs(point[1] - goal[1])
1140	
1141	    last_frame = len(frames) - 1 if frames is not None else None
1142	    last_cost_frame = len(cost_frames) - 1 if cost_frames is not None else None
1143	
1144	    def step_cost(point, t):
1145	        # Cost of entering ``point`` at time ``t``; the start cell is
1146	        # never entered. Time-varying frames take the value of frame
1147	        # ``t`` (the last frame persists); otherwise the static ``costs``
1148	        # matrix or unit steps apply.
1149	        if cost_frames is not None:
1150	            frame = (cost_frames[t] if t <= last_cost_frame
1151	                     else cost_frames[last_cost_frame])
1152	            return frame[point[1]][point[0]]
1153	        if costs is None:
1154	            return 1
1155	        return costs[point[1]][point[0]]
1156	
1157	    def frame_cells(t):
1158	        if frames is None:
1159	            return frozenset()
1160	        return frames[t] if t <= last_frame else frames[last_frame]
1161	
1162	    # Heap entries are (f, h, x, y, t, g, path, seen): f/h/x/y/t give the
1163	    # fixed numeric priority and candidates still tied are ordered by the
1164	    # complete coordinate path lexicographically, so ordering never depends
1165	    # on obstacle sets, in-frame coordinate order, or traversal order. The
1166	    # frozenset ``seen`` mirrors ``path`` for an O(1) repeat check and is
1167	    # never compared (distinct histories always differ in ``path``).
1168	    if state is None:
1169	        h0 = heuristic(start)
1170	        start_path = (start,)
1171	        open_heap = [(h0, h0, start[0], start[1], 0, 0, start_path,
1172	                      frozenset(start_path))]
1173	        closed_count = 0
1174	        expanded_nodes = [] if trace or snapshot else None
1175	        cost_limited = False
1176	        # Best goal closing seen so far, keyed exactly as the tie-break
1177	        # specializes at the goal: (g, t, path) (there f == g, h == 0 and
1178	        # (x, y) is fixed). Closing a goal does not stop the search
1179	        # immediately: an equally cheap route whose chain runs through
1180	        # higher-h nodes might still be undeveloped. Since each move costs
1181	        # at least 1 and the Manhattan h changes by at most 1 per move,
1182	        # f = g + h never decreases along a route; once the smallest f on
1183	        # the heap exceeds the best goal cost, no route of that cost (or
1184	        # less) can remain undiscovered.
1185	        best_key = None
1186	    else:
1187	        open_heap = state["open"]
1188	        closed_count = state["closed_count"]
1189	        expanded_nodes = state["expanded_nodes"]
1190	        best_key = state["best_key"]
1191	        cost_limited = state["cost_limited"]
1192	    budget_stop = False
1193	    has_status = max_expanded is not None or max_cost is not None
1194	
1195	    while open_heap:
1196	        if best_key is not None and open_heap[0][0] > best_key[0]:
1197	            break
1198	        if max_expanded is not None and closed_count >= max_expanded:
1199	            # Live route candidates remain but the budget is spent; close
1200	            # nothing more. A goal already closed still wins below.
1201	            budget_stop = True
1202	            break
1203	        _, _, x, y, t, g, path, seen = heapq.heappop(open_heap)
1204	        closed_count += 1  # every popped route node closes exactly once
1205	        if expanded_nodes is not None:
1206	            # Histories reaching the same (x, y, t) each record a triple,
1207	            # in the order their route nodes are actually closed.
1208	            expanded_nodes.append((x, y, t))
1209	        if (x, y) == goal:
1210	            goal_key = (g, t, path)
1211	            if best_key is None or goal_key < best_key:
1212	                best_key = goal_key
1213	            continue  # routes end at the goal; never expanded past it
1214	        next_t = t + 1
1215	        frame = frame_cells(next_t)
1216	        for dx, dy in _NEIGHBORS:
1217	            nx, ny = x + dx, y + dy
1218	            if not (0 <= nx < width and 0 <= ny < height):
1219	                continue
1220	            nxt = (nx, ny)
1221	            if nxt in obstacles or nxt in frame or nxt in seen:
1222	                continue  # static obstacle, timed obstacle, or revisit
1223	            new_g = g + step_cost(nxt, next_t)
1224	            if max_cost is not None and new_g > max_cost:
1225	                # The candidate's accumulated cost exceeds the limit:
1226	                # discard it and remember that a discard happened.
1227	                cost_limited = True
1228	                continue
1229	            new_path = path + (nxt,)
1230	            h = heuristic(nxt)
1231	            heapq.heappush(
1232	                open_heap,
1233	                (new_g + h, h, nx, ny, next_t, new_g, new_path,
1234	                 seen | {nxt}),
1235	            )
1236	        if (allow_wait and frames is not None and next_t <= last_frame
1237	                and (x, y) not in frame):
1238	            # Waiting in place: the route stays one more frame at no
1239	            # entering-cell cost. Only generated while the next time step
1240	            # still lies within the provided frames (after the last frame
1241	            # moves reuse it but no waits are generated), and only while
1242	            # the cell itself is free at that next frame. The coordinate
1243	            # is already in ``seen``, so the repeat check is untouched.
1244	            wait_path = path + ((x, y),)
1245	            h = heuristic((x, y))
1246	            heapq.heappush(
1247	                open_heap,
1248	                (g + h, h, x, y, next_t, g, wait_path, seen),
1249	            )

1251	        result = {"path": None, "cost": None, "expanded": closed_count}
1252	        if has_status:
1253	            result["status"] = _status_for(budget_stop, cost_limited)
1254	    else:
1255	        best_g, _, best_path = best_key
1256	        result = {
1257	            "path": list(best_path),
1258	            "cost": best_g,
1259	            "expanded": closed_count,
1260	        }
1261	        if has_status:
1262	            result["status"] = "found"

1264	        result["expanded_nodes"] = expanded_nodes
1265	    if snapshot and result.get("status") == "budget_exhausted":
1266	        result["checkpoint"] = _snapshot_checkpoint(

1268	            max_cost, closed_count, expanded_nodes,
1269	            _tree_snapshot_state(open_heap, best_key, "plan",
1270	                                 cost_limited, max_cost),

1278	                allow_wait=False, state=None, cost_frames=None):

1280	
1281	    This is the ``plan_any`` counterpart of ``_search_dynamic``. The only
1282	    semantic differences are: the heuristic is the minimum Manhattan

1285	    ``_search_dynamic`` the feasibility of a route depends on its exact

1287	    frames), so every node carries its complete path and routes reaching

1365	        closed_count = state["closed_count"]
1366	        expanded_nodes = state["expanded_nodes"]
1367	        best_key = state["best_key"]
1368	        cost_limited = state["cost_limited"]

1370	    has_status = max_expanded is not None or max_cost is not None
1371	
1372	    while open_heap:
1373	        if best_key is not None and open_heap[0][0] > best_key[0]:
1374	            break
1375	        if max_expanded is not None and closed_count >= max_expanded:
1376	            # Live route candidates remain but the budget is spent; close
1377	            # nothing more. A goal already closed still wins below.
1378	            budget_stop = True
1379	            break
1380	        _, _, x, y, t, g, path, seen = heapq.heappop(open_heap)
1381	        closed_count += 1  # every popped route node closes exactly once
1382	        if expanded_nodes is not None:
1383	            # Static mode records coordinate pairs, dynamic mode the
1384	            # (x, y, t) triple; distinct histories each record an entry in

1386	            expanded_nodes.append((x, y, t) if dynamic else (x, y))

1390	            if best_key is None or goal_key < best_key:

1411	                open_heap,
1412	                (new_g + h, h, nx, ny, next_t, new_g, new_path,
1413	                 seen | {nxt}),
1414	            )

1418	            # only within the provided frames and while the cell itself
1419	            # is free at the next frame. The coordinate is already in
1420	            # ``seen``, so the repeat check is untouched.

1422	            h = heuristic(cell)

1424	                open_heap,
1425	                (g + h, h, x, y, next_t, g, wait_path, seen),
1426	            )

1431	    else:
1432	        best_g, _, best_path = best_key
1433	        result = {
1434	            "path": list(best_path),
1435	            "cost": best_g,
1436	            "expanded": closed_count,
1437	        }
1438	        if has_status:
1439	            result["status"] = "found"

1441	        result["expanded_nodes"] = expanded_nodes

1443	        result["checkpoint"] = _snapshot_checkpoint(
1444	            "plan_any", width, height, obstacles, start, goals, costs,
1445	            frames, max_cost, closed_count, expanded_nodes,
1446	            _tree_snapshot_state(open_heap, best_key, "plan_any",
1447	                                 cost_limited, max_cost),
1448	            allow_wait, cost_frames,
1449	        )
1450	    return result
1451	
1452

1454	                         trace, max_expanded, max_cost=None, snapshot=False,
1455	                         allow_wait=False, state=None):
